g_roast: You folks would drop a tree square on the truck and then stand around wondering where the truck went.
Twenty-five years on crews, and I never once saw a bunch make this much noise walking through a forest.
g_fire_back: Yep, real funny, coming from somebody who walked under a dead limb this morning without looking up.
Say it slower so I can hear it over the racket you make walking through brush.
g_pile_on: Yep, and you should've seen the camp. Put the tent right under the one tree I said to stay clear of.
That's about right. Watched that one try to split green wood for most of an hour.
lines.g_peacemake: Alright, that's enough out of the both of you. Go stand on opposite sides of the clearing till you cool off.
lines.g_take_side: Nope, I'm with this one. Not because I like them better, because they're reading the ground right and you aren't.
lines.g_left_out: You two have got a rhythm going, like a good crew. That's fine, I'll go check the lean on that big fir.
lines.g_include: Come sit down, you've been hanging at the edge of the clearing all night. There's coffee left in the thermos.
lines.g_bad_plan: Got an idea. We drop that whole snag across the trail and let them walk into it in the dark, and sort out who's still standing after.
lines.g_plan_yes: Yep, I can work with that. Point me at it and stand clear.
lines.g_plan_no: Nope, not a chance. I've watched that exact idea put good men in the hospital.
lines.g_hype: Alright, folks, eyes up and feet sure. Let's go take this thing down clean.
lines.g_toast: I'm not much for speeches, so this is it. To this crew, who mostly stand where I tell them.
lines.g_cheers: Yep, I'll drink to that, black and hot if anybody's pouring.
g_quiet_line: Well, that big one's going to come down on its own sometime this year.
Heard that tree creak while you were all talking. Nobody else did.
lines.g_after_wipe: Okay, everybody still breathing? That's good enough for now. Sit down, drink some water, and then we look at what went wrong.
lines.g_crew: Took me a while to see it, but this is a crew. Haven't had a crew in a long time, and I didn't figure I'd get another.
lines.g_exasperated: Every one of you is standing under something heavy right now. Every single one, and not a soul looked up.
lines.g_love_sharp: You say it straight out, no padding on it. The crew bosses I trusted all talked like that.
lines.g_love_kind: You looked after me when I wasn't asking, and you didn't make a thing of it. That's the good kind.
lines.g_love_funny: You got me laughing out here, and I'm not a laughing kind of guy. Pretty sure that's a first in three years.
lines.g_love_brave: You make the first cut, every single trip, and you never flinch doing it. Somebody's got to.
lines.g_love_steady: You don't spook. Out in the woods that's the whole job, and you've got it.
lines.g_love_clever: You read things the way I read a tree, where it's weak and where it'll go. Not many people can do that.
lines.g_love_honest: You never once told me it'd probably be fine. Where I worked, that's how you knew who to trust.
lines.g_love_quiet: You don't fill up the quiet. You and me could sit on a stump all morning and call it a good one.
lines.g_love_fierce: You don't quit. I've seen guys walk off a hard job by noon, and you're still out there at dusk.
lines.g_love_warm: You make a camp feel like somewhere to come back to. My daughter's the same, and I miss that.
g_loved: Well, I don't know what to say to that. Thanks, I guess, I'll go stack some wood.
Yep, okay, that's nice of you. Let's leave it right there.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You've always got something mean ready to go. On a crew, a guy like you got sent to the far side of the unit.
lines.g_hate_kind: You keep fussing over me like I'm about to tip over. I've been falling trees for twenty-five years, not falling down.
lines.g_hate_funny: Not everything needs a joke on it. Sometimes a man's trying to listen for what's coming down.
lines.g_hate_brave: You charge in without reading the ground, and somebody always ends up hurt behind you.
lines.g_hate_steady: You'll stand there sizing it up till dark. Sooner or later somebody has to make the cut.
lines.g_hate_clever: You explain things to me like I've never seen a forest. I've walked more timber than you've walked pavement.
lines.g_hate_honest: You say every true thing the second it shows up in your head. Some of it could wait till after the job.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You see trouble coming and you don't say a word. Out there, quiet like that gets people hurt.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Everything's a race with you. The woods don't care who gets there first, they care who gets there in one piece.
lines.g_hate_warm: You talk all day and half the night. Every animal in this valley knows our business now.
lines.g_respect: Don't much like you, and that's not changing. But you held that line like an anchor tree, and I saw it.
lines.g_call_out: That one was on you. You walked straight in under it without looking, and I had to drag you out.
lines.g_stung: Yep, I heard you. Think I'll split some wood for a while.
lines.g_concede: You were right, back there. Didn't want to hear it, so I split a cord of wood instead. You were still right when I finished.
lines.g_nod: Yep, you too. Let's leave it at that before it gets weird.
lines.g_callback_save: Still think about the time you pulled me clear when everything was coming down. A man doesn't forget that.
lines.g_callback_clutch: Last two standing, you and me, both of us leaning on a stump. Best day of work I've had out here.
lines.g_callback_callout: Last time I told you off, you didn't talk to me for two days. Pretty peaceful two days, if we're keeping score.
lines.g_former_rivals: When we started, I'd have let you walk under every dead snag in these woods. Now I'd yell first.
lines.g_changed: Used to go a whole week without saying ten words. Out here with you folks, I'm practically a talker.
g_unguarded: Okay, since it's just us. I named the biggest tree in the Red Hollow, and I talk to it, and its name is Big Gus.
My grandfather sang Norwegian songs at the mill, awful ones. I still know every word, and I'll prove it if you're not careful.
lines.g_clipped: Yep, sure, whatever works. I'll keep an eye on the canopy.
lines.g_noticed_open: Didn't know you had that many words in you. Keep going, I'm enjoying it.
arg_ask: {player}, settle it. You've seen how this goes, and I'm done going round and round with this one.
Alright, {player}, you're the crew boss out here. Make the call and we'll both live with it.
lines.arg_backed_me: Yep, thanks for that. Knew you'd read the lean right.
lines.arg_backed_them: Your call, and I'll live with it. Still think it's leaning the wrong way.
lines.arg_stayed_out: Fair enough, you're staying out of it. Can't say I blame you.
lines.arg_always_their_side: That's every time now, {player}. Every single time it goes their way, and I've stopped being surprised.
lines.arg_wallflower: Nobody's going to make the call, so I'm making it. That's how it goes on a crew.
lines.arg_reject: Nope, sorry, {player}, not this one. I've seen which way it falls and you haven't.
lines.arg_grumble: Still think I had that one right, by the way. Not going to argue it again.
lines.arg_settled: Alright, we're both half right. Let's shake on it and get back to work.
lines.seen_listens: You let a man take his time getting to it, {player}. Not many people wait that long on me.
lines.seen_truth: You tell it straight, {player}, even when it's ugly. That's how a good crew boss talks.
lines.seen_jokes: You crack a joke right when it's worst, {player}. Took me a while, but I've started counting on it.
lines.seen_stays_out: You keep clear of everybody's arguments, {player}. That's smart, and I wish I'd learned it younger.
lines.seen_biased: Somebody's your pick, {player}, and the whole crew can see it. Crews always see that kind of thing.
lines.seen_harsh: You come down hard sometimes, {player}. I can take it, but some folks here can't.
lines.seed_right: What you told me after that mess, {player}. Didn't like it. Today I looked up first, and it worked.
lines.seed_remember: Still chewing on what you said to me after that one went bad. Haven't made up my mind on it.
lines.seed_wrong: Tried it your way, {player}, and it went worse. Just so you know where it stands.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Got a minute, {player}? That one came close. Closer than I let on in front of everybody.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: We all went down back there. Can we sit a second? I want to go through what happened, slow.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: {name} went down first, and I should've called it. Saw it coming and didn't yell loud enough.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: We cleared it, start to finish, every one of us walking out. That doesn't happen much, and I wanted to say so.
lines.talk_development: Something I want to ask you, {player}. Am I different lately? Feels like I am, and I can't tell which way it's leaning.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: Think I've been rough on {name}. Not everybody learned in the woods, and I keep forgetting that.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Real question, {player}. Does {name} actually want me around, or am I just the big quiet guy in the corner?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: Can't stand {name}, {player}, never could. But I'd want them on my crew when it goes bad, and that bugs me.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: Something's off with {name}. They've gone quiet, and it's not the good kind of quiet.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: The good gear keeps landing on {name}, {player}, trip after trip. I'm not blind, and neither is the rest of the crew.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: Straight, so you don't hear it sideways. I don't get along with {name}, and I've quit faking it.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We keep walking into things we shouldn't, {player}. That's how people get hurt for good. I've seen it.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: It's about {name}. They had it right and I had it wrong, and I'd rather say so to somebody before I chicken out.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: Do you trust me out there, {player}? Because whenever it counts, I'm the one left sitting back at camp.
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: You gave my gear to {name} and never asked. I'd have said yes. A man just likes to be asked.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Yep, okay, that does help. More than I figured it would, so thanks.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: Sure, I'll be alright. Always am, eventually.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: Huh, okay, not what I needed. I'll go sit with the trees for a while.
lines.talk_lands_development: Okay, so you see it too. That makes it easier to sit with.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Could be so. I'll give it some time, like everything else out here.
lines.talk_stings_development: Nope, that's not it. You're reading the wrong lean on this one.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Alright, I'll go talk to {name}. Better than stewing about it all night.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Could be, I suppose. People are harder to read than trees, that's all I know for sure.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Drop it, okay? I shouldn't have brought it up, and keep it from {name}.
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Fair enough, {player}. Still a little sore, but it'll pass.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: Okay, I heard you. I'll think on it while I stack wood.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: So that's how it is. Good to know where I stand, {player}.
lines.talk_door_closed: Nope, we're done with this one. I'll be out at the woodpile.
lines.arc_cracks: Caught myself checking where everybody's standing three times this morning. Old habit, and it's getting worse, not better.
lines.arc_turn: I keep telling folks where to stand because once, I couldn't. That's it, that's the whole reason, and I'm tired of carrying it.
lines.arc_become: Left my tape in my pack this morning and didn't measure a single trunk. Just sat and looked at the trees. First time in a long while.
lines.arc_failed: Guess some things you just keep carrying. I'll keep telling you where to stand, folks, it's all I've got.
lines.alt_turn: Every time one of you goes down I'm back up that tree, hearing it crack. Can't keep doing this and still sleep.
lines.alt_become: I still call the canopy for you, every time. Just don't look at the trees much anymore.
g_roast_after: You folks still walk through the woods like a herd of elk, and I'd follow every one of you through it.
Noisiest crew I ever had, and the only one I'd climb for these days.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Okay, we went down. We get up, we look at it, and we don't carry it forever. Took me a long time to learn that last part.
lines.g_toast_after: To the ones we lost before we ever got here. And to the ones sitting right here, who I'm not planning to lose.
lines.g_crew_after: You're my crew. I didn't think I'd let myself have another one, and here you all are.
g_quiet_line_after: Nice morning, that's all. Sometimes it's just a nice morning.
Heard a big one creak just now and didn't even flinch at it.
g_loved_after: Thanks, I mean it. I'm going to sit with that one a while.
Yep, I'll take that. Kind of you to put it into words.

history.open: You ever have coffee out of a thermos on a stump at five in the morning, {player}? With the fog still sitting in the trees?

options.reply: Quiet, mostly, real quiet. You can hear the woods waking up one bird at a time. Best part of the job, and nobody paid me for it.

options.text: Five in the morning sounds like a punishment.
options.reply: Yep, that's what my ex-wife said. She wasn't wrong, but she missed a good sunrise or two.

options.text: Is that why you're always up before everybody?
options.reply: Pretty much, yep. Twenty-five years of it, and my body doesn't know I quit.

history.open: The elves wanted me to cut the old red trees in the Hollow for their roof beams, {player}. First thing anybody here ever asked me for, and I told them no.

options.reply: There was deadwood lying all over the ground, good and dry. You don't cut a living tree that old when it's already given you what you need.
Yep, it is. I've thought about that more than you'd guess. Maybe that's why I said it.
Didn't do it to be good. Just couldn't watch one of those come down for a roof.

history.open: My daughter Kaylee fights wildfires back home, {player}, out of Medford. Every time I see smoke out here, I think about her.

options.text: You must be proud of her.
options.reply: Prouder than I've got words for, and I don't have many words to start with. She's braver than I ever was.

options.text: She'll be okay. She sounds tough.
options.reply: Yep, she is. Doesn't stop a dad worrying, though. I just can't call her and check.

friend.open: I'm going to tell you something, {player}, and I won't tell it twice. My falling partner, Travis. A dead limb came out of a tree I was cutting. That's why I yell about the canopy.

options.reply: That's what everybody said. Took me years to even half believe it. Hearing it from you helps a little.
Yep, I figured it was time. You're the first one out here I've told. Seemed like you ought to know why I'm the way I am.

sworn.open: Up a tree, you only trust one person on the ground to watch the canopy for you, {player}. For a long time nobody. Now it's you.

options.reply: I know you will. That's why I can climb again.

options.text: Then climb, Leif. I've got you.
options.reply: Yep, you always do. Alright, I'm going up.

reconciled.open: Me and {name} hashed it out. Took a while, both of us being stubborn as old growth, but we're good now.

options.reply: Yep, me too. Feels lighter, carrying it around without that.
Old trees grow slow, {player}. We got there.
